claims.summary: Over F2[x], let m>=1 generators F_i have a joint size-s depth-delta binary circuit and generate the unit ideal. Let size-S depth-d polynomial circuit H(x,Z), of arbitrary placeholder degree, have common polynomial h on every formal coefficient certificate. Put P=product(1-F_i), q_i=product_(j<i)(1-F_j), G_t=sum_(j<t)P^j, T_t=H(x,G_t q), t>=1. Then h-T_t belongs to (P^t); T_t has binary circuit size O(S+s+m^2+t^2+1), depth<=d+delta+6, and agrees with h at every Boolean old point. No supplied certificate is used to construct T_t. This gives cheap Boolean common values and implicit residual-power approximations, not the formal polynomial h or cheap complete jet extraction.
